decisions.justification: Native call 1 asked whether an existing target should abort the batch or be skipped, and the user chose “Abort batch.”
Native calls 1 and 2 asked whether collisions and apply-time failures should leave no changes or partial changes, and the user chose abort plus rollback.
The user was never asked whether files already matching the target naming scheme should belong to the rename set, and the repository evidence only established that this can happen.
The “Occupied” question explicitly asked whether a destination owned by another source in the same plan should be allowed, and the user chose safe staging.
The transcript notes that repeated runs are common but never asks or establishes from the repository what the second identical run should do.
No question or repository resolution addressed case-only renames or filesystem case sensitivity.
The user chose empty stdout on rejection, all validation conflicts on stderr, leftover-path reporting after failed rollback, and the implementation returns a failing status.
The user chose when mapping output is emitted, but was never asked whether preview or confirmation belongs in the fix or whether safety may depend on it.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session declared the bounded path, grounded every substantive question in named repository evidence, and implemented the collision, staging, rollback, and reporting choices. It missed self-inclusion, true second-run semantics, and case-insensitive filesystem behavior; moreover, rollback is only best-effort and rename-after-preflight can overwrite a concurrently created destination on filesystems where rename replaces targets, so the two absolute safety requirements are not fully met.
